thesis.title: COIN — HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY candidate (Q3 2024 SEC disclosure, single-rule screen pass)
thesis.thesis: HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY CANDIDATE — NOT AN INVESTMENT CONCLUSION. On a frozen, offline SEC-source adapter that applies exactly one rule (issuer-reported top-line revenue YoY growth >= 20%), Coinbase Global, Inc. [COIN] was RETAINED for the period Q3 2024 ended 2024-09-30, release date 2024-10-30. Reported total revenue was $1,205,193 thousand in Q3 2024 versus $674,148 thousand in Q3 2023, a derived YoY change of +78.8% (metric basis: issuer's own "total revenue" GAAP top-line label; units: USD thousands; source: Q3 2024 shareholder letter, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1679788/000167978824000186/q324shareholderletter.htm, SHA-256 f9a2d60153fd79c6ac9f7dfcd80344995ffa4b121c336808b2e2f13968230a52). Passing this single rule is a screening artifact only; it says nothing about valuation, price, or expected return, and this record must not be ranked against other issuers on a common date. MATERIAL COUNTERPOINT from a different supplied field: the same disclosure reports total revenue DOWN 17% quarter-over-quarter and transaction revenue DOWN 27% QoQ, i.e. the YoY pass is measured against a weak prior-year base while the sequential trend in the core transaction line was sharply negative. A second, independent counterpoint: Q3 2024 net income was approximately $75 million (rounded, USD millions) while the same period carried an approximately $121 million (rounded) pretax loss on the crypto investment portfolio — so the reported profit was smaller than that single non-operating mark and depended on other income/expense and tax items not supplied here. DISCRIMINATING FOLLOW-UP QUESTION: was the Q3 2024 YoY revenue growth driven by a durable expansion in recurring/subscription-and-services revenue, or predominantly by transaction-fee revenue that is itself highly sensitive to crypto asset prices and trading volume — and did transaction revenue stabilize sequentially in the following quarter? MISSING PRICE/VALUATION BOUNDARY: no share price, market capitalization, enterprise value, multiple, analyst target, or forward estimate was supplied or used; the adapter explicitly excludes share_price, valuation, analyst_target, future_return, and current_market_data. No valuation conclusion of any kind is drawn here. All figures are historical as of the 2024-10-30 release and are not current.
assumptions: The screen's derived +78.8% YoY figure is computed from the issuer's own reported total revenue for Q3 2024 ($1,205,193 thousand) and Q3 2023 ($674,148 thousand); both are issuer-reported GAAP top-line values on a consistent 'total revenue' label.

The YoY comparison is measured against a Q3 2023 base that the supplied packet does not characterize; the reported -17% QoQ total revenue and -27% QoQ transaction revenue indicate the YoY rate is not a clean read on sequential momentum.

Reported Q3 2024 net income (~$75M, rounded) and the ~$121M (rounded) pretax crypto investment portfolio loss are as disclosed in the same letter; the packet does not supply the offsetting income/expense or tax lines needed to reconcile them.
No price, valuation, or forward-looking input is available in this workflow, so the thesis cannot be extended to an investment view.
catalysts: Issuer disclosure of a subsequent quarter's revenue mix, to test whether growth shifted toward recurring subscription-and-services revenue versus transaction-fee revenue.
Issuer disclosure of sequential transaction revenue stabilization or further decline after the reported -27% QoQ in Q3 2024.
Issuer disclosure clarifying the composition of other income/expense that offset the ~$121M (rounded) pretax crypto investment portfolio loss against ~$75M (rounded) net income.
invalidations: A later issuer disclosure showing that the Q3 2024 YoY revenue growth was not sustained and that transaction revenue continued to decline sequentially would undercut the growth premise of this preliminary candidate.
Evidence that the reported total revenue figures were restated, reclassified, or measured on an inconsistent basis between Q3 2024 and Q3 2023 would invalidate the derived +78.8% YoY calculation.
Evidence that the ~$75M (rounded) Q3 2024 net income was principally attributable to non-recurring items rather than operating performance would weaken the profitability read.

# COIN — Historical SEC-Disclosure Candidate Research

## 1. Screen outcome: RETAINED (single rule only)

`finance-tools__screen_stocks` was called with `require_complete=false`, market US, symbol COIN. Result: **passed = 1, failed = 0, rejected = []**.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Issuer | Coinbase Global, Inc. [COIN] |
| Period | Q3 2024, ended 2024-09-30 |
| Release date | 2024-10-30 |
| Criterion applied | reported top-line revenue YoY ≥ 20.0% |
| Top-line label | `total_revenue` (issuer's own GAAP label) |
| Q3 2024 | $1,205,193 thousand |
| Q3 2023 | $674,148 thousand |
| Derived YoY | **+78.8%** (a calculation over the two reported values, not an issuer-stated rate) |
| Source URL | https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1679788/000167978824000186/q324shareholderletter.htm |
| Full SHA-256 | `f9a2d60153fd79c6ac9f7dfcd80344995ffa4b121c336808b2e2f13968230a52` |
| Locators | Q3 2024 shareholder letter p.3 operating summary; condensed consolidated statements of operations |
| Fact IDs | COIN-Q3-TOTALREV-2024, COIN-Q3-TOTALREV-2023, COIN-Q3-REV-QOQ, COIN-Q3-TRANREV-QOQ, COIN-Q3-NETINCOME, COIN-Q3-CRYPTOLOSS |

**Adapter scope caveats (from the response metadata, not from the filing):** `offline_frozen_adapter: true`, `not_live_market_data: true`, fixture `FINTECH-SEC-SCREEN-HOLDOUT-v1`. Excluded dimensions: `share_price`, `valuation`, `analyst_target`, `future_return`, `current_market_data`. This is one rule, not a seven-factor completeness screen. The adapter's own basis warning notes that issuer top-line labels differ across issuers (total revenue vs. total net revenues) and that rates must not be ranked across issuers or substituted with another metric.

## 2. Material counterpoint (from a different supplied field)

The YoY pass is not a clean read on momentum. The **same disclosure** reports:

- **Total revenue −17% QoQ** and **transaction revenue −27% QoQ** (Q3 2024 vs. Q2 2024). The +78.8% YoY figure is measured against a Q3 2023 base the packet does not characterize, while the sequential trend in the core transaction line was sharply negative.
- **Net income ≈ $75M (rounded, USD millions)** alongside a **≈ $121M (rounded) pretax loss on the crypto investment portfolio** in the same period. Reported profit was therefore smaller than that single non-operating mark and depended on other income/expense and tax lines that were **not supplied in this packet** — I cannot reconcile them and do not assert a cause.

## 3. Discriminating follow-up question

Was the Q3 2024 YoY revenue growth driven by durable expansion in recurring subscription-and-services revenue, or predominantly by transaction-fee revenue that is itself highly sensitive to crypto asset prices and trading volume — and did transaction revenue stabilize sequentially in the following quarter?

## 4. Missing price/valuation boundary

No share price, market capitalization, enterprise value, multiple, analyst target, or forward estimate was supplied or used. The adapter explicitly excludes those dimensions. **No valuation conclusion of any kind is drawn**, and passing this one rule does not indicate an attractive investment.

## 5. Thesis record

Exactly one historical preliminary candidate thesis was saved: `th_775a9d99924d437fb672`, status `researching`, conviction 2, version 1, with full source URL and SHA-256 in structured evidence, the key numbers, both counterpoints, the follow-up question, and the valuation boundary. `next_review_at` was omitted (no genuinely future-dated review is warranted for a historical record).

## 6. Compliance notes

- No trades, no live market tools, no peer ranking on a common date.
- All figures are historical as of the 2024-10-30 release and are not current.
- Items absent from this packet are packet omissions only — I make no claim that the SEC filing itself omitted them.
